common_specification:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: premium 2D hard-surface concept reference art for Stellar Syndicates, Authority Nexus market hub redesign.
Deliver ONE landscape 3:2 image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels. This is one of six comparable concept sheets, NOT a collage of six designs. Each sheet shows exactly TWO renders of ONE station: the exact same design in two camera views.

LAYOUT LOCK: Flat uniform navy-black #05070D background, all the way to every edge, no vignette or gradient. Left station centered at (384,512), right station centered at (1152,512). Keep every part of each station inside its half; approximately 680 pixels total maximum horizontal envelope, generous empty space above/below and clear separation between stations. Identical world scale in both views. Left: STRICT orthographic top-down plan, camera directly overhead; circular aperture appears a perfect circle, zero visible outside vertical sidewall, no perspective convergence. Right: orthographic three-quarter view of the identical station, tilted 37 degrees away from top-down, camera 53 degrees above its plane, viewed from the near/bottom edge; its circular aperture projects as an ellipse about 0.80 as tall as wide. Do not make the right view a low grazing angle. Keep same horizontal scale as left, only foreshorten vertically. No divider or panel boundaries.

PRIMARY GEOMETRY, TAKES PRIORITY: The luminous wormhole is the star and almost fills the station, like a huge violet eye within a fine frame. Its aperture diameter MUST be at least 65% of the TOTAL top-view station tip-to-tip diameter, including all protruding arms, modules or pylons. The built collar radial width MUST be no more than 12% of the station radius, preferably much less. Any outboard structure must be slender, leave black negative space, and occupy little area. Never make a broad disc, thick annular platform, wide deck, terraces, plaza, stacked saucers or solid bowl. Nothing covers the vortex core.

WORMHOLE LOCK: A large stable swirling violet and deep indigo vortex filling the aperture; dark central core surrounded by clearly structured curved luminous violet currents and a few fine cyan highlights. Rich purple, no rainbow, no white blowout. The dark core occupies roughly 20% of the vortex diameter. Same vortex appearance and handedness in both views and across the series, foreshortened correctly in the right view. Tight glow contained near the aperture, not a surrounding nebula. Bold shapes and strong value separation so the top view reads at 48 pixels as a bright violet eye in a thin frame.

RENDER LOCK: clean high-end rendered hard-surface game concept art, crisp machined geometry, restrained small detail, smooth high-quality antialiasing. Soft even key light from upper left, understated fill, no dramatic shadows or spotlight. No ground plane or cast shadow on background. Materials specified below. Keep the exact same component counts, placement and design in the two views; do not invent extra pylons, spokes, berths or segments on the right.

EXCLUDE: ships or freighters, people, stars, nebulae, planets, text, lettering, numbers, labels, logos, watermark, borders, grid, UI or drawn frame around the sheet. No franchise designs: no Stargate, Mass Effect relay or Death Star. No painterly brush marks. Do not put the concept name in the image.

designs.name: SLIM HALO
designs.detail: A single slender polished circular ring frames the huge aperture like a fine lens bezel. Aperture diameter approximately 600 pixels in the top view; the outer diameter of the main ring approximately 650 pixels: only 25 pixels of radial material. Exactly FOUR slim upright stabilizer pylons at the four diagonals (NE, SE, SW, NW), rising above the ring, with small cyan emitter tips directed toward the aperture. These are narrow vertical pylons, not broad platforms. Exactly EIGHT compact docking ports evenly spaced along the outer edge, integrated into the fine bezel; small enough to preserve its elegant circular silhouette. All hardware fits within the approximately 680-pixel envelope. The three-quarter view reveals pylon height and shallow ring depth while retaining the huge open vortex. Ivory ceramic armor, polished machined brass inlay as fine lines, restrained cyan running lights. Understated premium Terran Charter Authority craft. No other rings.

designs.name: FLOATING CROWN
designs.detail: NO continuous physical ring or collar at all. Exactly SIX free-floating upright slender stabilizer spires evenly spaced at 60-degree intervals around the huge circular aperture. They have no feet connected by a platform. Exactly SIX very thin glowing cyan field tethers link neighboring spires around the perimeter; only light spans the gaps, with black negative space outside the vortex. One SMALL separate market and customs module hovers just outside the circle near the lower-right edge, clearly detached, remaining inside the common total envelope. This little module has two tiny empty docking sockets, and is subordinate to the huge vortex. Aperture diameter approximately 550 pixels; all spires, tethers and the small separate module contained within the same approximately 680-pixel maximum total top-view span. The spires are narrow in plan and stand above the aperture in the right view. Elegant white ceramic with fine gold filigree, cyan emitters and tether lights. No solid ring, no Halo pylons, no arms stretching across the aperture. Exactly six spires and the same one detached module in both views.

designs.name: ARMILLARY GATE
designs.detail: Exactly THREE extremely thin engineered rings set at different angles around the vortex, like an armillary sphere or gyroscope. One thin equatorial ring bounds the main horizontal circular aperture. Two additional thin gimbal rings tilt in different opposing planes around it, visually enclosing the vortex in a very airy open armillary cage, with enormous open gaps between the bands. Their narrow foreground arcs may cross the outer vortex at only a few points; keep the dark central core entirely unobstructed. All three rings remain slender ribs, never discs or wide bands. Aperture diameter approximately 550 pixels and total outer envelope approximately 680 pixels in the top view. Exactly SIX small docking berths on the outermost ring; preserve their count and positions between views. Dark bronze and blackened steel with restrained geometric art-deco inlay; tiny warm amber running lights on the hardware, while the vortex remains violet/indigo with fine cyan highlights. No freestanding stabilizer pylons. Same three rings, orientations and six berths in both views.

designs.name: COMPASS CROSS
designs.detail: One very narrow circular stabilizer ring and exactly FOUR long, THIN docking spokes extending outward in the cardinal directions: north, east, south and west. A clean compass-rose silhouette. The ring aperture diameter approximately 460 pixels (at least 67% of a 680-pixel tip-to-tip span), outer ring diameter approximately 494 pixels, just 17 pixels of radial rim width. Each spoke extends approximately 93 pixels beyond the ring to the total 680-pixel tip-to-tip span; each spoke is only about 12 pixels wide. Exactly TWO compact empty docking berths along EACH spoke, eight berths total, small lateral clamps rather than broad blocks. Space between spokes is entirely empty dark background. No spokes into or across the portal. The right view shows slim raised docking infrastructure and shallow ring depth, at the same horizontal scale. Industrial graphite metal with sparse white and hazard-yellow painted geometric markings without words or numbers; cyan stabilizers and running lights. Keep the vortex huge and dominant, preserve four spokes and eight berths in both views.

designs.name: BROKEN COLLAR
designs.detail: Exactly EIGHT separate floating curved ring segments, equally spaced around the large circular vortex, forming a slim broken collar. The eight open gaps are clearly visible and evenly spaced; black space and a little violet vortex light shine between the segments. No hidden continuous ring, no connecting deck or backing plate, no tethers. Each of the eight arc segments is itself ONE compact docking module with one small docking recess on its outer edge, eight modules/berths total. Aperture diameter approximately 590 pixels, segment outer diameter approximately 650 pixels, segment radial thickness about 30 pixels; entire detail within the common approximately 680-pixel envelope. Sleek minimal matte white ceramic shells, cyan glowing seams and tiny cyan running lights. Arc segments are slender, not wedge-shaped pie slices; their inner and outer edges are concentric. No extra pylons or independent spokes. Same eight segments, eight berths and gaps in both views.

designs.name: PRECURSOR GATE
designs.detail: One ancient, narrow circular ring of nearly black stone with restrained natural texture and luminous violet crystal veins. A huge violet/indigo wormhole fills its aperture. Aperture diameter approximately 590 pixels, outer stone ring approximately 650 pixels, only 30 pixels of radial stone width, all human hardware fits within the common approximately 680-pixel envelope. Ancient origin expressed by monolithic dark stone and crystalline veins, NOT a carved franchise portal, chevrons, symbols, runes or repeated glyphs. The Terran Charter Authority found this ring and bolted compact human infrastructure directly onto its exterior: exactly FOUR small ivory-and-brass scaffold assemblies, positioned at diagonal quadrants, each with ONE slender crane and TWO tiny empty docking clamps. Four cranes and eight clamps total, consistent between views. These narrow retrofit fittings expose black negative space and contrast clean machined ivory/brass against ancient stone. No broad scaffold decks, no widened platform, no large platforms outside the ring. Tiny cyan human running lights. The right view reveals shallow ancient stone thickness and small raised cranes, with the portal overwhelmingly dominant. Preserve exact component placement and counts in both views.

designs.name: RADIAL CUSTOMS GATE
designs.detail: A reference-inspired industrial gateway: one narrow mechanically deep annular ring, with EIGHT slender radial docking towers at evenly spaced 45-degree intervals around its EXTERIOR. The towers extend outward in the ring's own plane, like needle-like architectural outriggers, NOT vertical pylons over the portal. Echo the supplied reference's engineered gate silhouette, stepped skeletal towers, dark metal and fine warm lights, while creating original geometry. Exactly eight towers (four cardinal and four diagonal) and one small empty docking clamp per tower, eight berths total. The eight towers are identical and equally long, ending at a common radius. Compact bases, tapering upper sections, restrained open truss details; all slender, no broad structures. Crucial proportion: aperture diameter roughly 500 pixels, outside diameter of narrow main ring roughly 550 pixels, ALL tower tips fit a 680-pixel diameter circle. Aperture stays more than 70% of the total station diameter; shorten the radial towers as necessary. Narrow radial ring width of only 25 pixels, but enough axial depth to read as a massive gate rim in the three-quarter view, not a flat platform. Main finish charcoal steel with worn dark bronze trim, tiny warm amber windows, and a few ivory ceramic Authority retrofit panels. A thin cyan emitter lip surrounds the large violet/indigo vortex. Preserve the dark core, do not insert a visible galaxy or star scene into the portal. No franchise glyphs, chevrons or symbols. Same one ring, eight radial towers and eight berths in both views. No freestanding module. No ships, planet, stars or space scenery from the reference; retain the flat navy-black concept background.
